full_goal_assessment.current_result: A reproducible, bounded methodological study of acceleration diagnostics, prescribed learning-rate clocks and whole-run randomness controls. It has research and practical audit value as a technical/methodological note.
full_goal_assessment.novelty_status: Original measurements under this declared protocol are supported. A substantial new scientific mechanism, new statistical method, or established priority over closely related work is not demonstrated. The targeted literature audit is insufficient to certify novelty of the complete empirical story.
full_goal_assessment.scope_preservation: The original goal remains mechanisms and conditions of double descent across model families. R10-R12 concern a methodological slice, primarily train-loss acceleration in CatBoost. R13 graphics/packaging improves reproducibility but does not fill the missing scientific questions or justify redefining the user goal as complete.
concrete_scientific_gaps: No newly established interpolation-aligned held-out-risk double-descent effect with capacity and optimization axes separately controlled in both MLP and GBDT. R12 classification interpolation times do not themselves test risk-peak shape, shift or mechanism.
Known linear noise/ridge/early-stopping/tree-averaging controls fromR2-R5 remain controls, not a new cross-model explanatory result or clear advance over Kanoh/Nakkiran/Curth.

No reproducible natural late event was established by the declared R12 gate, and whole-run random_strength does not intervene specifically on annealing. Explaining an unestablished natural event would be premature.

R10 compares repository rules and a calibrated custom scan on a finite analytic catalog. There is no strong published slope-change baseline implementation/comparison under matched assumptions, and no validated false-alarm transfer to actual model-training trajectories.

R11 schedule/clock dependence is an informative positive control built from known optimization facts; its sign reversal is not evidence of a new GBDT mechanism. R12 maximum-score shifts can reflect early dynamics and range normalization.

Two small environments, one synthetic generator and one fixed real corpus do not establish broad practical generalization, model-family transfer or independent-corpus robustness. Twelve seed units and t intervals also leave distributional adequacy uncertain.

The historical Qwen baseline/corpus proximity/metadata questions remain unresolved. Excluding that corpus is appropriate for current claims but does not mean the earlier audit requests were completed.
No demonstrated downstream benefit beyond the audit protocol itself, and no independent external replication, comprehensive novelty assessment or evidence supporting publication-level significance.
full_goal_assessment.bounded_next_research_question: After a faithful small replication of the closest published GBDT split-candidate setting, does an interpolation-aligned held-out-risk peak persist when model capacity and optimization progress are varied separately in MLP and CatBoost, and does a predeclared clock/schedule intervention change that relation? Use a bounded train-only discovery/preflight to establish an informative capacity bracket, then an independent frozen confirmation with measured train errors/residuals, held-out shape criteria, paired interventions and explicit no-effect/non-identifiable outcomes. Do not enlarge the menu until a desired curve appears. First state the prediction that distinguishes the proposed result from the closest published explanation; do not treat another known peak as novelty.
full_goal_assessment.continuation_recommendation: Close and release R13 only as a reproducibility milestone. Keep the broader research goal incomplete and continue an explicitly frozen scientific branch addressing the original mechanism/generalization question within existing authority and budgets.
